column1: Across cultures, wisdom has been considered one of the most revered human qualities.
column2: 在不同文化中，智慧一直被视为人类最受尊崇的品质之一。

column1: Although the truly wise may seem few and far between, empirical research examining wisdom suggests that it isn’t an exceptional trait possessed by a small handful of bearded philosophers after all — in fact, the latest studies suggest that most of us have the ability to make wise decisions, given the right context.
column2: 真正明智的人似乎屈指可数，但有关智慧的实证研究表明，智慧终究不是少数蓄着胡须的哲学家独有的非凡特质。事实上，最新研究显示，只要情境合适，大多数人都有能力作出明智的决定。
column3: few and far between|少之又少
column7: a small handful of|极少数的
column11: make wise decisions|作出明智的决定

column1: ‘It appears that experiential, situational, and cultural factors are even more powerful in shaping wisdom than previously imagined,’ says Associate Professor Igor Grossmann of the University of Waterloo in Ontario, Canada.
column2: “经验、情境和文化因素在塑造智慧方面，作用似乎比以前想象的还要大，”加拿大安大略省滑铁卢大学副教授伊戈尔·格罗斯曼说。
column3: experiential|adj. 与个人经历有关的
column4: situational|adj. 与具体情境有关的

column1: ‘Recent empirical findings from cognitive, developmental, social, and personality psychology cumulatively suggest that people’s ability to reason wisely varies dramatically across experiential and situational contexts.
column2: “认知心理学、发展心理学、社会心理学和人格心理学近期的实证发现综合起来表明，人们明智推理的能力，会随经历和情境的不同而发生很大变化。
column5: developmental|adj. 发展的；发展心理学的

column1: Understanding the role of such contextual factors offers unique insights into understanding wisdom in daily life, as well as how it can be enhanced and taught.’
column2: 了解这些情境因素的作用，有助于我们从独特的角度认识日常生活中的智慧，以及如何提升和传授这种智慧。”

column1: It seems that it’s not so much that some people simply possess wisdom and others lack it, but that our ability to reason wisely depends on a variety of external factors.
column2: 看来，与其说有些人有智慧、另一些人没有，倒不如说，我们能否作出明智推理，取决于多种外部因素。

column1: ‘It is impossible to characterize thought processes attributed to wisdom without considering the role of contextual factors,’ explains Grossmann.
column2: “如果不考虑情境因素的作用，就不可能说清楚被视为智慧表现的那些思考过程，”格罗斯曼解释道。

column1: ‘In other words, wisdom is not solely an “inner quality” but rather unfolds as a function of situations people happen to be in.
column2: “换句话说，智慧不单是一种‘内在品质’，它还会随人恰好身处的情境而展现出来。
column7: as a function of|随……而变化
column8: happen to be in|恰好身处

column1: Some situations are more likely to promote wisdom than others.’
column2: 有些情境比另一些更容易激发智慧。”

column1: Coming up with a definition of wisdom is challenging, but Grossmann and his colleagues have identified four key characteristics as part of a framework of wise reasoning.
column2: 为智慧下定义并不容易，不过格罗斯曼和同事归纳出了明智推理框架中的四个主要特征。

column1: One is intellectual humility or recognition of the limits of our own knowledge, and another is appreciation of perspectives wider than the issue at hand.
column2: 其一是在认知上保持谦逊，也就是承认自身知识的局限。其二是能看到超出眼前问题的更广阔视角。

column1: Sensitivity to the possibility of change in social relations is also key, along with compromise or integration of different attitudes and beliefs.
column2: 同样关键的还有：能敏锐地察觉社会关系可能发生变化，以及能在不同态度和信念之间作出妥协或加以整合。

column1: Grossmann and his colleagues have also found that one of the most reliable ways to support wisdom in our own day-to-day decisions is to look at scenarios from a third-party perspective, as though giving advice to a friend.
column2: 格罗斯曼和同事还发现，要让我们自己的日常决定更明智，最可靠的办法之一，就是从第三方的视角审视情形，如同在给朋友出主意。

column1: Research suggests that when adopting a first-person viewpoint we focus on ‘the focal features of the environment’ and when we adopt a third-person, ‘observer’ viewpoint we reason more broadly and focus more on interpersonal and moral ideals such as justice and impartiality.
column2: 研究显示，采用第一人称视角时，我们会关注“环境中的焦点特征”；采用第三人称的“旁观者”视角时，我们的思考范围更广，也会更关注公正和不偏不倚等人际和道德理想。
column9: reason more broadly|从更广的角度思考

column1: Looking at problems from this more expansive viewpoint appears to foster cognitive processes related to wise decisions.
column2: 从这种更开阔的视角看问题，似乎有助于促进与明智决策相关的认知过程。

column1: What are we to do, then, when confronted with situations like a disagreement with a spouse or negotiating a contract at work, that require us to take a personal stake?
column2: 那么，当我们面临与配偶意见不合或在工作中谈判合同这类与自身利害相关的情形时，该怎么办？

column1: Grossmann argues that even when we aren’t able to change the situation, we can still evaluate these experiences from different perspectives.
column2: 格罗斯曼认为，即便我们无法改变处境，仍然可以从不同的视角评估自己的经历。

column1: For example, in one experiment that took place during the peak of a recent economic recession, graduating college seniors were asked to reflect on their job prospects.
column2: 例如，一项实验在不久前一次经济衰退最严重的时候进行。研究人员请即将毕业的大学四年级学生思考自己的就业前景。
column5: peak|n. 高峰；最严重的阶段
column7: graduating college seniors|即将毕业的大四学生

column1: The students were instructed to imagine their career either ‘as if you were a distant observer’ or ‘before your own eyes as if you were right there’.
column2: 研究人员请这些学生用两种视角之一想象自己的职业生涯：一种是“仿佛你是远处的旁观者”，另一种是“用自己的眼睛去看，就好像你就在现场”。
column8: before your own eyes|亲眼所见

column1: Participants in the group assigned to the ‘distant observer’ role displayed more wisdom-related reasoning (intellectual humility and recognition of change) than did participants in the control group.
column2: 在被分配为“远处的旁观者”的那一组，参与者比对照组表现出更多与智慧有关的推理，例如在认知上保持谦逊，以及认识到事物会变化。
column7: wisdom-related reasoning|与智慧有关的推理
column9: recognition of change|对变化的认识

column1: In another study, couples in long-term romantic relationships were instructed to visualize an unresolved relationship conflict either through the eyes of an outsider or from their own perspective.
column2: 在另一项研究中，长期交往的伴侣被要求想象一场彼此之间尚未解决的矛盾。他们或是从局外人的眼光去看，或是从自己的角度去看。
column3: long-term romantic relationships|长期伴侣关系
column8: through the eyes of|以……的眼光

column1: Participants then discussed the incident with their partner for 10 minutes, after which they wrote down their thoughts about it.
column2: 随后，参与者和各自的伴侣就这件事讨论了10分钟，接着写下自己的想法。

column1: Couples in the ‘other’s eyes’ condition were significantly more likely to rely on wise reasoning — recognizing others’ perspectives and searching for a compromise — compared to the couples in the egocentric condition.
column2: 采用“他人视角”的伴侣明显更倾向于运用明智推理，也就是体会他人的立场并寻求折中；而从自身角度出发的伴侣就较少这样做。

column1: ‘Ego-decentering promotes greater focus on others and enables a bigger picture, conceptual view of the experience, affording recognition of intellectual humility and change,’ says Grossmann.
column2: “跳出自我视角，会让人更关注他人，能从概念和大局层面来看待自身经历，也更能认识到自身知识有限、事情会发生变化，”格罗斯曼说。
column3: Ego-decentering|n. 自我去中心化；跳出自我视角

column1: We might associate wisdom with intelligence or particular personality traits, but research shows only a small positive relationship between wise thinking and crystallized intelligence and the personality traits of openness and agreeableness.
column2: 我们也许会把智慧与智力或某些人格特质联系起来；但研究显示，明智思考与晶体智力，以及与开放性、宜人性这两项人格特质，都只呈微弱的正相关。

column1: ‘It is remarkable how much people can vary in their wisdom from one situation to the next, and how much stronger such contextual effects are for understanding the relationship between wise judgment and its social and affective outcomes as compared to the generalized “traits”,’ Grossmann explains.
column2: “同一个人在一种情境和另一种情境中，展现出的智慧可以相差很大，这令人惊讶。同样令人惊讶的是，要理解明智判断与它带来的社会和情感后果之间的关系，情境的作用比宽泛的‘特质’要强得多，”格罗斯曼解释道。
column5: from one situation to the next|从一个情境到另一个情境

column1: ‘That is, knowing how wisely a person behaves in a given situation is more informative for understanding their emotions or likelihood to forgive [or] retaliate as compared to knowing whether the person may be wise “in general”.’
column2: “也就是说，知道一个人在特定情境下的行为有多明智，比知道他‘总体上’是否明智，更有助于理解他的情绪，以及他有多大可能选择宽恕或报复。”
